a.onclick: openModal( this, "Prime Editing Guide RNA (pegRNA)", ["42015509"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42015509"], ["The prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA) is an extended version of the conventional sgRNA. In addition to the spacer and scaffold regions required for Cas9 targeting, it contains a Primer Binding Site (PBS) and a Reverse Transcription Template (RTT). These additional elements encode the desired genetic modification and provide the template used by the reverse transcriptase to directly rewrite the genomic DNA sequence."])

openModal( this, "Prime Editor (PE) mRNA", ["42015509"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42015509"], ["Prime Editor mRNAs encode a Cas9 nickase fused, through a flexible linker, to an engineered Moloney Murine Leukemia Virus (M-MLV) reverse transcriptase. Following translation, the protein associates with the prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA) to form an active editing complex capable of introducing all transition and transversion substitutions, as well as small insertions and deletions, without generating double-strand DNA breaks or requiring donor DNA templates."])

openModal( this, "Double-Strand DNA Cleavage", ["38308006"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38308006"], ["After complete pairing between the sgRNA and its DNA target, Cas9 undergoes a conformational rearrangement that activates its nuclease domains. The HNH domain cleaves the DNA strand complementary to the guide RNA, whereas the RuvC domain cleaves the opposite strand, generating a double-strand DNA break approximately three nucleotides upstream of the PAM sequence."])

openModal( this, "Repair by Cellular Pathway", ["38308006"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38308006"], ["The double-strand break generated by Cas9 activates endogenous DNA repair pathways. In the absence of a repair template, the break is predominantly repaired through Non-Homologous End Joining (NHEJ), an error-prone mechanism that frequently introduces insertions or deletions capable of disrupting gene function. When an exogenous donor DNA template is provided, the cell can instead employ Homology-Directed Repair (HDR) to introduce precise sequence modifications at the target locus."])

openModal( this, "Targeting Binding", ["38308006"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38308006"], ["Genome editing begins with recognition of the Protospacer Adjacent Motif (PAM), a short DNA sequence immediately flanking the target site. For Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, the PAM sequence is 5'-NGG-3'. Cas9 continuously scans genomic DNA until it encounters a valid PAM, at which point it locally unwinds the DNA duplex. The sgRNA spacer then hybridizes with the complementary DNA sequence, ensuring that cleavage occurs only at the intended genomic locus."])

openModal( this, "Reverse Transcription", ["42015509"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42015509"], ["The engineered reverse transcriptase uses the Reverse Transcription Template (RTT) encoded within the pegRNA to synthesize a new DNA strand containing the desired genetic modification. Rather than copying an RNA genome, the enzyme directly writes the edited DNA sequence into the target genomic locus."])

openModal( this, "Flaps Compete for Incorporation", ["42015509"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42015509"], ["Reverse transcription generates a transient edited DNA flap that competes with the original unedited strand. Endogenous DNA repair enzymes preferentially incorporate the edited sequence while removing the original flap, completing genome editing without generating double-strand DNA breaks or requiring exogenous donor DNA templates."])

openModal( this, "Base Editor mRNA", ["41606292"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41606292"], ["Base Editor mRNAs encode genome editors capable of chemically modifying individual DNA bases without introducing double-strand DNA breaks. Two major classes have been developed: Cytosine Base Editors (CBEs), which convert C•G into T•A, and Adenine Base Editors (ABEs), which convert A•T into G•C. The present figure illustrates the Adenine Base Editor used in the Baby KJ case study. The editor consists of a Cas9 nickase fused to an evolved TadA adenine deaminase, allowing precise base conversion while minimizing indel formation and genotoxicity."])

openModal( this, "Clinical Application: Baby KJ", ["NEJMoa2504747"], ["https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2504747"], ["Baby KJ represents the first personalized CRISPR-based therapy developed specifically for a single patient. The treatment employed an adenine base editor delivered as lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA to correct a pathogenic mutation in the CPS1 gene responsible for carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I deficiency. By converting a single A•T base pair into G•C without introducing a double-strand DNA break, the therapy demonstrated the clinical feasibility of rapid, patient-specific in vivo genome editing for the treatment of ultra-rare genetic diseases."])

openModal( this, "Nuclear Localization Signal (NLS)", ["34022911"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34022911"], ["The Nuclear Localization Signal (NLS) is a short peptide enriched in lysine and arginine residues that is specifically recognized by the importin α/β transport machinery. Its function is to direct Cas9, Base Editors and Prime Editors from the cytoplasm into the nucleus, where genome editing takes place. Modern genome editors frequently incorporate two or three NLS sequences to maximize nuclear import efficiency and increase editing activity."])

openModal( this, "Cas9 mRNA", ["38308006"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35798006"], ["Cas9 mRNA encodes the Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 nuclease, which is translated in the cytoplasm following release from the lipid nanoparticle. Newly synthesized Cas9 associates with the single guide RNA (sgRNA) to form an active ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex of approximately 190 kDa (~160 kDa for the Cas9, ~32kDa for the sgRNA). Guided by Nuclear Localization Signals (NLS), the complex is actively transported through the nuclear pore complex into the nucleus, where Cas9 introduces a site-specific double-strand DNA break (DSB). This break subsequently activates endogenous DNA repair pathways, including Non-Homologous End Joining (NHEJ) and Homology-Directed Repair (HDR)."])

openModal( this, "Single Guide RNA (sgRNA)", ["38308006"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35798006"], ["The single guide RNA (sgRNA) is a synthetic RNA molecule that combines the CRISPR RNA (crRNA) and the trans-activating CRISPR RNA (tracrRNA) into a single transcript. It consists of a ~20-nucleotide spacer sequence, specifically designed to be complementary to the target DNA, and a conserved scaffold region that folds into stem-loop structures required for Cas9 binding. While the spacer determines the genomic target, the scaffold stabilizes the Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complex and enables efficient DNA recognition and cleavage. The sgRNA is used in both CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing and Base Editing."])

openModal( this, "Single-Strand DNA Cleavage", ["41606292"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41606292"], ["Unlike wild-type Cas9, the Cas9 nickase used in base editors contains an inactive RuvCnuclease domain while retaining an active HNH domain (configuration given by the Cas9 nickase featuring a D10A mutation), allowing cleavage of only one DNA strand. This single-strand nick stimulates endogenous mismatch repair mechanisms that preferentially replace the unedited DNA strand using the edited strand as a template, thereby increasing editing efficiency while avoiding the formation of double-strand breaks."])

openModal( this, "Targeting Binding", ["41606292"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41606292"], ["As in conventional CRISPR-Cas9 editing, the Cas9 nickase first recognizes a PAM sequence and is guided to the target locus by the sgRNA. DNA binding locally opens the double helix, exposing a short single-stranded DNA region known as the editing window, within which the target adenine becomes accessible to the TadA deaminase."])

openModal( this, "Targeting Binding", ["42015509"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42015509"], ["Prime editing begins with PAM recognition and guide RNA-directed binding of the Cas9 nickase to the target genomic locus. Following local DNA unwinding, the spacer hybridizes with the complementary DNA sequence while the Primer Binding Site and Reverse Transcription Template remain positioned to direct the subsequent DNA synthesis reaction."])

openModal( this, "Single-Strand DNA Nicking", ["42015509"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42015509"], ["The Cas9 nickase introduces a single-strand break approximately three nucleotides upstream of the PAM sequence. The newly generated 3' DNA end then hybridizes with the Primer Binding Site (PBS) contained within the pegRNA, creating the primer required for reverse transcription."])

openModal( this, "Adenine Deaminase", ["41606292"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41606292"], ["The evolved TadA adenine deaminase catalyzes the hydrolytic deamination of adenine into inosine within the exposed DNA strand. Although inosine is not a natural DNA base, it is interpreted by the cellular replication and repair machinery as guanine, ultimately enabling a permanent A•T to G•C base substitution."])

openModal( this, "Repair by Cellular Pathway", ["41606292"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41606292"], ["Following adenine deamination, the modified DNA strand is processed by endogenous DNA replication and repair pathways. During these processes, inosine is recognized as guanine, leading to the permanent conversion of the original A•T base pair into G•C. Since no double-strand DNA break or donor DNA template is required, base editing substantially reduces the risk of large insertions, deletions and chromosomal rearrangements."])

openModal( this, "Nuclear Pore Complex", ["30883195"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30883195"], ["The Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC) is a large protein assembly embedded within the nuclear envelope that regulates the selective transport of macromolecules between the cytoplasm and nucleus. It is composed of cytoplasmic filaments, a central transport channel lined by FG-nucleoporins (F= Phenylalanine; G= Glycine), and a nuclear basket. Cas9-containing ribonucleoproteins are too large to diffuse passively through the pore and therefore rely on active transport mediated by importin α/β, which recognizes the exposed Nuclear Localization Signals on the editing proteins."])

openModal( this, "Lipid Nanoparticle–mRNA", ["35798006"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35798006"], ["For in vivo editing, the genome editor is delivered as mRNA encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) rather than as purified protein. This has become the standard route for reaching internal organs such as the liver: pre-formed ribonucleoprotein can be electroporated into cells only ex vivo, whereas whole organs cannot, and LNPs efficiently carry mRNA to hepatocytes following intravenous injection. Because a single mRNA molecule is translated into many copies of the editor, comparatively little material must be delivered to reach a therapeutic dose. mRNA is also produced rapidly and inexpensively by in vitro transcription and reprogrammed simply by altering its sequence-advantages that allowed the Baby KJ therapy to be designed, manufactured, and administered within roughly six months of diagnosis."])
